response.message:
I've drawn an AWS knowledge assistant for support staff. Staff sign in through Cognito, the web app on CloudFront calls API Gateway, and a Lambda gathers context from the ticket, approved knowledge and a read-only CRM lookup. The Lambda then writes a draft with citations using Bedrock, and drafts it can't support go to a person through an SQS escalation queue. The CRM connection is read-only, so it never issues refunds or changes customer records.

For the first local test, the emulator would run the generated code against mocked AWS services, sample tickets and canned model replies. That checks the flow, how sign-in is enforced and how escalation is routed. It doesn't check real answer quality, whether the model is approved for use, IAM, or your region or account access. Those still need a real Bedrock evaluation in your own account. Nothing has been deployed or verified.

How should it find relevant knowledge: matching keywords across a small set of approved articles (up to about 100), or searching by meaning across a larger library?

proposal.title: AWS support-staff knowledge assistant (first sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: support staff draft grounded replies from synthetic tickets, approved knowledge and read-only CRM records, and escalate uncertain cases to a person. Assumptions: the region is not selected yet. The retrieval mode is still open, so typed implementations are not bound yet. Integrations with the existing ticket queue and CRM need engineering. No automatic refunds or record changes. The diagram shows design intent only and is not deployment evidence.

data.label: Support staff browser
data.description: Support agents using a browser. Client reference only; not provisioned.

data.label: Staff web app
data.description: Staff interface: shows the ticket, the drafted reply with citations and an Escalate button. The app owns its private static assets.

data.label: Staff sign-in
data.description: Staff sign-in with MFA. Its tokens authorize API calls and carry the staff role used for retrieval filtering.

data.label: Assistant API
data.description: Authenticated HTTP API. No anonymous access.

data.label: Draft orchestrator
data.description: Loads the ticket and runs authorized retrieval from approved knowledge plus a read-only CRM lookup. It then drafts a cited reply, abstains or escalates when the evidence is weak, and returns the draft to the staff app. It has no refund or write tools.

data.label: Approved knowledge catalog
data.description: Approved articles with ACLs and revisions. The retrieval mode (keyword or semantic) is still to be decided.

data.label: Synthetic ticket queue
data.description: Existing synthetic ticket system. Read integration still needs engineering.

data.label: Existing CRM
data.description: Customer records. Read-only access only; the assistant never modifies records or issues refunds.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: Drafts the grounded reply. Model ID, access, quotas and region are still to be verified.

data.label: Human escalation queue
data.description: Holds low-confidence or out-of-scope cases for a human agent to review.

data.label: Audit logs
data.description: Logs requests, cited sources, abstentions and escalations. Retention is still to be agreed.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents harmful financial or data changes caused by model error or prompt injection.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Never issue refunds or modify customer records automatically."
requirementDrafts.statement: The assistant must never issue refunds or modify customer records. CRM access is read-only, and any customer-affecting action is taken by a person.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Avoids leaking restricted knowledge or customer data in drafts.
requirementDrafts.statement: Retrieval returns only approved knowledge and customer records that the signed-in staff member is allowed to see. Unknown identities fail closed.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Keeps unsupported answers away from customers.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "grounded answer drafting ... and human escalation"
requirementDrafts.statement: Every draft cites its sources. When the evidence is insufficient, the assistant abstains and routes the case to human escalation.

response.message:
The good news is that the check found no failures, and the access boundaries we drew all hold together, including the read-only CRM and the escalation path. It's blocked because 8 components don't have a generated implementation yet: the web app, sign-in, API, orchestrator and catalog still need code, and the existing browser, ticket queue and CRM each need a plan for how we reference or connect to them. I won't hide any of that or call the setup validated. A supported setup only exists if we choose keyword search, and even then the ticket and CRM connections and the escalation would stay as product engineering work.

Should the assistant find answers by matching keywords across a small set of approved articles (up to about 100), or by searching for meaning across a larger library?
